Boy Taken Into Care Over Parents' Smoking

Well I guess it makes sense if, as the article says, the parents aren't even acknowledging it's a problem. But then, how dangerous is the smoke? I don't know. Probably a bit. Anyone got a strong opinion on this?

Likely, there are other concerns with the boy's care and this is just another layer of justification for removing him from the home. I grew up in a house where my mom smoked. I didn't have any breathing or allergy troubles and rarely got sick growing up. That's only anecdotal, though. Just because the smoking didn't trigger adverse health affects in me doesn't mean they didn't here. People are built differently. I do smoke as an adult, though. I guess honestly, I don't have a strong opinion either way, but if the boy was getting sick and the parent's weren't doing anything about it, the boy should have been removed and not specifically for the smoke. Specifically for the fact that the parents didn't give a shit about his health.

I spent years thinking that I had really bad motion sickness in cars, to the point that going for a drive longer than about 10 minutes was something I really didn't want to do. It seemed like every time I was in the car, I was nauseated and wanting to throw up. Childhood road trips were an additional layer of hell aside from the hours of boredom.

Turns out that I don't really get motion sickness at all. What I really had was a horrible time dealing with the fact that both of my parents smoked like coal fired locomotives and they were essentially hotboxing the shit out of me on every occasion we went anywhere in the car. Riding in a car with someone smoking still makes me ill.

We have a similar problem in the USA where Child Protective Services in some locations are looking for reasons to take your kids away, and nosy neighbors will report you for anything that they don't like.
Yes because they get money for each child they take.

The article says that the smoke was just one factor amongst many which led to the child being put up for adoption; however it fails to mention the other factors. If these are clearly negligent parents then I suppose this isn't unwarranted, but the article doesn't give us enough details.
